items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 27, 2013 [interview 2 of 2]…
items.q: And then along comes Wynton, who’s — gee I mean on one level he’s playing his far out music, on another level he’s playing so far in New Orleans music, march music.

ctx.x: Sonny Rollins, I don’t know why I can’t think, Sonny Rollins. He was playing all the time, but he had sort of gone underground. I mean people didn’t hear these people. Coltrane is dead I think already, and so all of a sudden people like Stan Getz and Scott Hamilton, and Zoot Sims were sort of becoming heroes again. And it was very communicative, easy to understand music. And the public said oh, all right, I can understand that. So a lot of people who didn’t know, could understand it. So they started to embrace it…
